requirements.title: Expression characteristics are determined recursively from syntax, operators, and primaries
requirements.definition: The type, type parameters, and shape of an expression depend on the operators and on the types, type parameters, and shapes of the primaries used in the expression. Those characteristics are determined recursively from the expression's syntactic form, and the expression type is either an intrinsic type or a nonintrinsic type.

pending.operator-and-primary-characteristics: PENDING positive-control source shape combining a literal primary, a named designator primary, and a numeric intrinsic operator so that the result's type, kind, and shape are attributable to the operands and operator. The plan cites the owners of the primary alternatives and intrinsic operation interpretation, and observes only the combined characteristics owned here.
pending.recursive-syntactic-characteristics: PENDING positive-control source shape with nested parenthesized and binary subexpressions whose final assignment context and explicit SHAPE/LEN/KIND inquiries distinguish the characteristics obtained by recursively applying the subexpression rules. The oracle must not infer evaluation order from the nesting.
pending.intrinsic-expression-type-domain: PENDING positive-control source shape producing integer, real, complex, logical, and character expressions in typed contexts. The intrinsic type definitions remain 7.4 dependencies, and KIND/LEN inquiries are used only to observe required characteristics.
pending.nonintrinsic-expression-type-domain: PENDING positive-control source shape using a derived-type constructor or defined operation result assigned to a declared derived-type variable and checked by a literal component value. Derived-type formation and assignment semantics remain dependencies; this facet observes that an expression type may be nonintrinsic.

requirements.oracle: Observe expression characteristics through valid typed contexts, assignment to declared destinations, and standard inquiries whose expected values are required by cited source rules rather than assumed from a processor's usual kind set.

They must not rely on compiler agreement, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted assembly, undefined reads, or floating-point value comparisons sensitive to mathematically equivalent rewrites permitted elsewhere in clause 10.

requirements.title: Polymorphic primaries and defined operations propagate declared and dynamic expression properties
requirements.definition: If an expression is a polymorphic primary or a defined operation, the expression has the same type parameters and declared and dynamic types as that primary or defined operation. Otherwise its type parameters and dynamic type are the same as its declared type and type parameters; in those non-exception cases the standard refers to them simply as the expression's type and type parameters.

pending.polymorphic-primary-declared-and-dynamic: PENDING positive-control source shape with a polymorphic allocatable or pointer primary whose dynamic type is distinguished by SELECT TYPE and a literal component oracle. The declared type, dynamic type, and type parameters are attributed to the primary owner and observed here only as the expression's propagated properties.
pending.defined-operation-declared-and-dynamic-t: PENDING positive-control source shape defining an operation that returns a polymorphic or type-parameterized result and then observing the result through SELECT TYPE or type-parameter inquiry. The defining function and generic resolution remain 10.1.6/15.4 dependencies.
pending.nonpolymorphic-dynamic-type-equals-decla: PENDING positive-control source shape using a nonpolymorphic intrinsic or derived-type expression in a typed assignment and, where derived, SAME_TYPE_AS or SELECT TYPE with a literal component oracle. The case must not claim any dynamic dispatch effect.
pending.simple-type-parameter-terminology: PENDING source-accounting control records that later catalogues may say 'type and type parameters' for non-exception expressions. A future fixture may include a nonpolymorphic character expression with explicit LEN/KIND checks, but this facet itself supplies no separate runtime effect beyond the p2 terminology.

requirements.oracle: Use dynamic-type observations only where the source requires a dynamic/declared distinction. Do not infer dynamic type from storage representation or compiler diagnostics; use standard type-selection or inquiry mechanisms with independently required expectations.

review_rationale: batch104: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). Reviewer read all 18 base units of 10.1.9.1, 10.1.9.2 and 10.1.9.3 in the original PDF rather than the author summary, verified 18 base / 49 fine units, 24 requirements and 81 facets (all pending), and independently confirmed the accounting claim that the packet newly accounts only 10 base units rather than 18: the eight numbered units R1025, C1007, R1026, C1008, R1027, C1009, R1028 and C1010 were already accounted by the numbered-rule inventory, and the reviewer verified each is neither double-counted nor dropped. The four permission dispositions were each checked and accepted: the 10.1.9.2 p3 disassociated-pointer phrase only allows contexts explicitly permitted elsewhere, and the three 10.1.9.3 p4 processor-dependent result-kind choices are not promoted to requirements. On the known mixed-kind trap the reviewer derived the rules independently before comparing: integer with real or complex uses the real or complex operand kind; different-range integer pairs require the greater RANGE kind and different-precision real or complex pairs the greater PRECISION kind; but equal-range integer, equal-precision real or complex, and different-kind logical results require only that the kind be one of the operand kinds, with the choice processor dependent. No pending plan hard-codes a kind value, predicts which operand kind is selected, or assumes that multiple nondefault kinds exist; plans compare KIND, LEN, RANGE and PRECISION against declarations, operands or dynamically discovered supported kinds. Vacuity was checked: LEN is explicit for character length, disassociated and unallocated arrays are given no SHAPE oracle, and the binary-operation shape plan warns that two conformable arrays cannot discriminate the x1-shape rule. No table is a base unit in this scope; Table 10.2 is cited as a dependency of already-registered 10.1.5.1 and not duplicated. Decision: source-eligible, no blocking findings; two non-blocking observations recorded in doc/source_audits/batch_104.json. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
